ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The image shows a regular hexagon. A center point is connected to two adjacent bottom vertices, forming a triangular sector. The triangle side from the center to a vertex is labeled 12 ft, the base is labeled 12 ft, and a 60° angle is indicated, supporting that this sector is an equilateral triangle. The figure also shows the base divided by the height into two 6 ft parts. Reasoning: The perimeter given by the text is 72 ft. Since the hexagon is a regular hexagon, all 6 sides are equal, so each side is 72 ÷ 6 = 12 ft. A regular hexagon can be decomposed into 6 congruent equilateral triangles, each with side length 12 ft. The area of an equilateral triangle is A = (√3/4)s² = (√3/4)(12²) = 36√3 ≈ 62.35 square feet. Multiplying by 6 triangles gives 6 × 62.35 ≈ 374.1 square feet.

raw_record.question_text: Find the area of a regular hexagon with perimeter 72 feet.

method.method_draft: Use the regular-hexagon decomposition route. Read from the text that the perimeter is 72 ft, so each of the 6 equal sides is 72/6 = 12 ft. Read from the image that the hexagon is regular and can be split into 6 congruent equilateral triangles (the 60° geometry supports this). Then find the area of one equilateral triangle with side 12 using A = (sqrt(3)/4)s^2, giving (sqrt(3)/4)(12^2) = 36sqrt(3) ≈ 62.35. Multiply by 6 triangles: 6 × 62.35 ≈ 374.1 平方英尺.
